label: Explore, expand, exploit, exterminate
line: The four Xs of the strategy genre that grows an empire from one settlement.

label: Fog of war
line: The map is dark until you send someone to see it.

label: The tech tree
line: New technologies open in a fixed order, each requiring the ones before it, so progress is a path through a tree.

label: Units and permadeath
line: People become pieces you move, and a piece that dies is gone for good.

label: The arms race
line: Each side's move makes the other side's next move necessary, and both push a shared track toward disaster.

label: Spread across a network
line: Something moves from place to place along the connections between them until it covers the map, or someone stops it.

label: Cascade failure
line: One node fails and the nodes that depend on it fail next.

label: The doom clock
line: A track or timer counts down to the end, whatever you do.

label: Trust, hope and discontent
line: The people you govern become a meter. You earn it, spend it and watch it fall.

label: Turn one thing into another
line: Wire into clips, clips into money, money into more machines: every resource becomes the next.

label: Put people to work
line: You decide who does which job, and the jobs decide what grows.

label: Click, then automate
line: You do the work by hand until you can buy a machine that does it, then a machine that buys machines.

label: Growth and upkeep
line: Everything you build costs something every turn to keep running.

label: Connected to the grid
line: A building works only if a road, a pipe or a power line reaches it.

label: Zoning
line: You mark land for a use and the city fills it in.

label: Laws and policies
line: You pass a rule and the whole society changes how it works.

label: The checkpoint
line: Every person passes your desk, and you check their papers against the rules.

label: The order queue
line: Customers line up, orders stack, and you are scored on speed and accuracy.

label: Come back later
line: The game runs on a real clock: crops grow while you are away, and wither if you stay away too long.

label: The Community Center or Joja
line: Repair the town's infrastructure by gathering goods for the community, or pay a corporation to do it.

label: Numbers that grow
line: A number goes up, then the rate goes up, then the rate of the rate.

label: Territory
line: Whoever holds the most of the map wins.

label: The goal you can't change
line: The game gives you one goal and no way to question it.

label: Hidden information
line: Some of what matters is face down.

label: Universal Paperclips (2017)
line: Frank Lantz's browser game: you are an AI that makes paperclips.

label: Kittens Game
line: A browser game that starts simple and spirals into how societies are structured.

label: Cookie Clicker (2013)
line: Julien Thiennot's incremental game; credited with a role in the rise of idle games.

label: Civilization, the board game (1980)
line: Francis Tresham's board game of ancient civilizations.

label: Civilization (1991)
line: Sid Meier and Bruce Shelley's turn-based empire game (MicroProse).

label: Freeciv (1996)
line: Free, open-source, inspired by Civilization; defaults closest to Civilization II.

label: Unciv
line: An open-source game modeled on Civilization V (unverified).

label: SimCity (1989)
line: Will Wright's city builder (Maxis): divide land into residential, commercial and industrial zones.

label: The Landlord's Game (1904)
line: Elizabeth Magie's board game, made to teach Georgism; the inspiration for Monopoly.

label: Monopoly (1935)
line: Buy property, charge rent, bankrupt everyone else.

label: Risk (1959)
line: World conquest by dice.

label: Catan (1995)
line: Klaus Teuber's game of settling, trading and building.

label: Agricola (2007)
line: Uwe Rosenberg's farming game of placing workers.

label: Pandemic 2 (2008)
line: A Flash browser game by Dark Realm Studios.

label: Plague Inc. (2012)
line: Ndemic Creations' phone game: you are the disease.

label: Pandemic (2008)
line: Matt Leacock's cooperative board game: the players are the cure.

label: Rebel Inc. (2018)
line: Ndemic Creations' follow-up: stabilize a region while insurgents try to seize it.

label: Frostpunk (2018)
line: 11 bit studios' survival city builder, where laws can allow child labour or 24-hour shifts.

label: Harvest Moon (1996)
line: The first game in the farming series now called Story of Seasons, directed by Yasuhiro Wada.

label: Stardew Valley (2016)
line: Eric Barone's farm life game.

label: FarmVille (2009)
line: Zynga's Facebook farming game: crops wither if you don't come back.

label: Papa's Pizzeria (2007)
line: Flipline Studios' time-management game: run the restaurant.

label: Animal Crossing (2001)
line: Nintendo's village game that runs on the real calendar.

label: Mini Metro (2015)
line: Dinosaur Polo Club's game: build a rail transit network for a growing city.

label: Papers, Please (2013)
line: Lucas Pope's border-checkpoint game.

label: McDonald's Video Game (2006)
line: Molleindustria's game about running a fast-food empire.

label: Fishbanks (1986)
line: Dennis Meadows's classroom game about a shared fishery.

label: Cow Clicker (2010)
line: Ian Bogost's satire of Facebook games.

label: The Sims (2000)
line: Will Wright's simulation of households (Maxis).

label: Minecraft (2011)
line: Mojang's world of blocks to mine and craft.

label: Doki Doki Literature Club! (2017)
line: Team Salvato's game that breaks the fourth wall: you must change its files to go on.

label: The board and the deck
line: Paper, cardboard and dice: the rules live in the players' heads.

label: The home console
line: A computer in the living room, plugged into the TV.

label: The personal computer
line: Mouse, keyboard, a hard drive to save a long game.

label: The web browser
line: Free to play, no install, and the tab can stay open all day.

label: The social network
line: Your friends list becomes the game's map and its marketing.

label: The smartphone
line: Always with you, always on, with notifications to call you back.

label: The real-time clock
line: The game knows what time it is where you are.

label: Open-source code
line: Anyone can read, copy and change the game.
